claim.property: Prototype integrity and rejection of reserved-token reads/writes across the core JSON Pointer data-to-runtime boundary
claim.attacker: Lower-trust JSON/SpecStream producer or path/value supplier, without arbitrary same-process JavaScript authority
claim.scope: Contract A4 and changed core API/README claims: decoded __proto__, constructor and prototype tokens rejected by core path utilities, stores/adapters and core SpecStream, with both path/from guarded before compound mutation
assumptions: Ordinary JSON state/spec objects and arrays, with no host-installed accessor/proxy or explicit reference to a shared prototype
Producer controls its supplied spec/state and element definitions; no restricted per-path authorization capability is documented
Host owns adapter callback implementations, component registry code and any downstream persistence authorization
distinctions: Core A4 security protection is supported. The literal claim that every legacy renderer rejects every reserved token is not supported: SEC-004 records a local dictionary-prototype exception, and SEC-002 records compound rejection defects.
No deployment-specific remote unauthenticated access, tenant isolation, service availability or privileged persistence property is inferred.
A1-A3, F1/F2, Test Strength and Resilience are not converted into security blockers without a demonstrated new authority or boundary.
